title: security: rbac-v2 enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Harden RBAC v2 enforcement around customer-managed KMS keys to guarantee data residency and prevent accidental cross-region key usage. This PR implements an enforceable policy path (enforce mode) and keeps a backwards-compatible audit-only mode for initial rollout. It also improves audit logging for KMS operations so security teams can reliably trace key usage and region decisions.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds RBAC v2 policy checks that validate KMS key region metadata against resource region/residency policies and deny requests violating residency constraints when enforcement is enabled.
- Enhances audit logging to include KMS key ARN, requested region, resolved key region, policy decision (allow/deny), and the RBAC rule id/version. Logs are structured and routed to the existing audit pipeline.
- Introduces a feature flag and admin-controlled rollout path: config.feature_flags.kms_region_pinning_mode = [audit|enforce]. Default is "audit" for the initial rollout.
- Adds server-side validators and API-level validation for create/update flows and runtime enforcement at serving request decision points.
- Adds integration tests and unit tests for the policy engine and audit payloads, plus docs for operators.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests updated 
[x] Integration tests added 
[x] Docs (security/kms-region-pinning.md) updated 
[x] Feature flag + migration plan included 
[x] Linear/Jira links provided (ENG-4821, SEC-312, SUP-2103)

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Deploy with default audit mode enabled across staging and prod. Collect logs for 2 weeks and run regression checks.
2) Enable enforce mode for a small set of orgs behind a toggle and monitor for denials and customer impact.
3) Gradually expand enforce mode while providing a bypass workflow for verified legacy keys.

Notes and limitations: This PR focuses on region pinning for AWS KMS and the platform's canonical KMS metadata. GCP/CMEK follow-ups are tracked in ENG-4922. During audit mode, policy decisions are logged but do not block requests. Enforcement requires a migration window and operator coordination.

If there's any remaining concern about latency, the policy check is designed to be cacheable per-key for short TTLs and performed before expensive serving paths.
